stem: The graph of $y = a\cos\theta + q$ is sketched for $\theta \in [0^\circ, 360^\circ]$. On this interval the greatest value of $y$ is ${=top}$ and the least value of $y$ is ${=bot}$, and the graph passes through the point $(0^\circ, {=k})$. Find the value of $a$.
solution: The graph oscillates between its least value ${=bot}$ and its greatest value ${=top}$, so its midline $y = q$ is halfway between them: $q = ({=top} + {=paren(bot)}) \div 2 = {=q}$.
The amplitude is the distance from the midline to the greatest value: $|a| = {=top} - {=paren(q)} = {=amp}$.
At $\theta = 0^\circ$, $\cos\theta = 1$, so $y = a + q$ there. The graph passes through $(0^\circ, {=k})$, so $a + {=paren(q)} = {=k}$.

So $a = {=k} - {=paren(q)} = {=a}$. This agrees with $|a| = {=amp}$, and its sign shows the reflection: $a$ is positive when the graph starts at its greatest value and negative when it starts at its least value.
notes: Advanced: the book's own inverse problem (read a and q off the features of a graph, here given in words because the stem cannot carry a diagram) with the twist that the sign of a must be decided from where the graph starts. Half the instances have a > 0 (the point at 0 degrees is the greatest value), half a < 0 (it is the least value); a is a whole number from -6 to 6, never 0, and q is a whole number, never 0. Checked numerically over the whole parameter space: greatest and least values of the sampled curve equal q + |a| and q - |a|, midline (top+bot)/2 = q, amplitude top - q = |a|, and k - q = a. The data are consistent and determine a uniquely.
